title: Epic: guided builds — tell people how to make a wall
description: The catalog is good at finding a named piece and bad at telling someone what to print. Invert the blueprint: instead of a part declaring what it accepts, a guide declares a thing you want to build and the parts that make it, driven by data rather than code. First slice is 'how do I make a wall?' end to end, covering build|s2w, build|wall on tile and build|separate wall. Design, with the verified state of the existing data model, is docs/design/guided-builds.md. Decisions already taken with Devon on 2026-09-19: guides are repo fixtures loaded into a table (admin editor later); the output is a parts list with downloads plus a shareable URL; wall only for the first slice; and the synthesised base slot comes out of the parser. The reason for that last one was first written as 'connection|openforge already implies a base', which review proved false across the catalog — 4,368 records carry the tag and only 2,455 have a base slot. The true rule is per method: within build|separate wall the slot and the tag are the same fact (1,220 of 1,221 openforge walls, and none of the 115 separate-wall floors), within build|thick wall likewise for the openforge walls carrying component|wall (87 of 100). Where the base goes is also per method and is NOT 'under the floor' in general: separate wall puts it under the wall, wall on tile under the floor (295 floors, no walls), s2w with the wall (no s2w floor carries a slot; the composition blueprints put fulfills: base on the wall part), and s-system nowhere. Any UI that replaces the synthesised slot has to read the build method, not just the connection tag. Feature slots (door, torch, lintel...) stay and are a later phase, so the model must not preclude them.
notes: Where the base goes is per method and is not 'under the floor' in general (PR #238 round 5): separate wall puts it under the wall (1,220 of 1,221 openforge walls carry the slot, 0 of 115 floors), wall on tile under the floor (295 floors, no walls), s2w with the wall (no s2w floor carries a slot; the composition blueprints put fulfills: base on the wall part), and s-system nowhere. Any UI that replaces the synthesised slot has to read the method.

title: [guided builds] Resolution engine in Python
description: Pure function: guide document plus a selection map in, resolved parts and the steps now reachable out. No HTTP, no database access in the core — candidate lookup is injected so the engine stays testable. src/CLAUDE.md is explicit that real logic belongs in Python, and this is real logic. Three things settled during design review: (1) the recommendation must be deterministic or the shareable URL does not reproduce what the person saw — the separate-wall wall role leaves 2,278 candidates on the literal query and 1,221 once prefer:connection|openforge is applied, and that prefer list ranks none of those 1,221 above another, so extend prefer until it totally orders and state the final tie-break (blueprint_name is the existing sort and the obvious one); (2) guides do NOT use constrain — it has no Python implementation, its real semantics include parent:false, siblings and filter-as-exclusion, and the thing it buys (every role the same size) is better asked than inferred, so size is a step and every role's composed query requires the chosen size|width|* outright; (3) composition rule: the composed query is the union of the method's tags, the role's query and any active refinements, each predicate list concatenated, with deny beating require — the engine knows nothing about the 177 dual-shape (shape|wall + shape|floor) pieces, and a guide that does not want a combined print denies the other shape in that role's query. A role whose composed query matches nothing resolves to no part and says so rather than silently dropping out. Unit tested against the real wall fixture, including options that beget options and options that remove them.

title: Propagate thingiverse sync data to AWS prod (fixture + API upsert path)
description: The tool runs against the LOCAL Postgres, but prod (AWS Lambda + serverless Postgres) is populated by replaying fixture JSON through the Flask API (bin/upload_fixture with OPENFORGE_BASE_URL, same pattern as blueprint fixtures). Thingiverse data (blueprint_id <-> thing_id mapping, public thing URLs) must ride that path so the app can render Thingiverse links in prod and support deeper integration later. Deliverables: fixture format for thingiverse mappings (exported from the local sync tables), an authenticated API upsert endpoint in the Flask app, and upload_fixture support. Note: prod likely only needs the mapping/links, not the per-file hash ledger — that is local operational state; decide the split when designing the fixture.
notes: DESIGN NOTE from PR #225 review: the schema allows one blueprint to appear in MULTIPLE things (partial unique index is per-thing only, and test_same_source_allowed_in_different_things pins that behavior). The prod fixture mapping is therefore 1:N — (blueprint_id, thing_id, public_url) derived per thingiverse_files row, not a unique-per-blueprint map. The app's Thingiverse links UI must handle a blueprint linking to several things.

title: [guided builds] guides table, fixture format and loader
description: New schema version: a guides table holding the guide document as jsonb keyed by a short key. Fixture format is YAML in openforge/db/fixtures/guides/, loaded by the existing fixtures command the way tag_descriptions is, with an OpenAPI schema beside the others in openforge/openapi/schemas/ so a malformed guide fails loudly and names the offending step. See docs/design/guided-builds.md for the document shape: steps with options, roles with tag queries and a prefer list, refinements with a declarative when: predicate over earlier selections.
notes: Reconciled with 'fulfills' rather than inventing a parallel mechanism. 'fulfills' is used 41 times in two positions that mean different things: 21 at the root of a blueprint (7 in cut-stone.json, 14 in dungeon_stone.json) saying this whole piece satisfies a slot of that name, and 20 entries across 18 of the s2w composition blueprints saying one part satisfies a sibling part's slot — the wall that is its own base. The guide format expresses the second without a new mechanism: an option lists the roles its build needs, so a method whose wall is its own base simply does not list the base role. The declarative when: predicate covers the options-beget-options half. Decided while implementing: option.roles is a map of role name to predicate (null for none) rather than a list, because a method is not one tag — the composites put build|s2w on the floor, build|separate wall on the wall and deny build|s2w on the base; option.tags remains as the shorthand for what is true of every role the option names. Toggle refinements are spelled on_tags/off_tags because bare on/off are YAML 1.1 booleans.

title: Sync engine: diff local files vs remote hashes, reconcile
description: For each managed thing: diff manifest-directed local files against remote files by normalized-MD5 comparison (via the thingiverse_files ledger) -> upload new, replace changed, delete removed, patch drifted metadata. Idempotent; dry-run mode showing planned actions before mutating. ALSO IN SCOPE: adopt/backfill existing Thingiverse things into the ledger by matching remote files to catalog blueprints by MD5, so things created outside the tool (or in prior manual runs) are recognized and never duplicated (see NOTES for the proven recipe + open decisions). Remote hash confirmed = content-MD5.
notes:
VALIDATED on real data (thing:7364110): Thingiverse file hash = content-MD5 (NOT SHA-256). Two compare requirements: (1) hash encoding VARIES — old things hex MD5 (32ch), recent base64 MD5 (24ch, e.g. lma97RnU7yEQDMZcDe1vEA==); normalize before compare (24-char/b64 -> decode to hex; 32-char -> lowercase; see client.normalize_hash). (2) Thingiverse SANITIZES filenames on upload (strips #, comma, etc). Match files by MD5, NEVER by name.

ADOPTION (added scope — proven manually 2026-07-08, must be reproduced in ad5):
ad5 must ADOPT existing Thingiverse things into the ledger, not only create new ones — otherwise it will create DUPLICATES of things made outside the tool or in prior runs. Recipe validated on 9 things / 347 links this session:
- GET /users/me/things (newest); select by criterion (published-year / --since date).
- Per thing: get_thing_files -> normalize_hash -> match to blueprints.file_md5 (UNIQUE, so md5->blueprint is 1:1).
- Upsert thingiverse_things (thing_id unique; status from is_published; published_at from `added`; last_synced_at=now) ON CONFLICT (thing_id).
- Rebuild thingiverse_files matched rows (blueprint_id), dedup per (thing, blueprint). Idempotent.
- A blueprint can map to MULTIPLE things (20 shared seen — e.g. bases across releases); per-thing uniqueness only, do NOT assume 1:1.
NOTE: a manual adoption snapshot already exists in the DEV DB only (9 things, 347 links). ad5 adoption must be idempotent so re-running over it is safe.

OPEN DECISIONS ad5 must resolve (the manual one-off punted on these):
- Non-catalog remote files (zips, gallery images): the thingiverse_files CHECK requires blueprint_id|image_id|local_path; an adopted remote-only zip/image has none of these. Either relax the CHECK to allow remote-only rows (remote_file_id set), or track only catalog-matched files. The manual run recorded matched MODEL files ONLY (skipped zips/images).
- remote_metadata_hash baseline for adopted things: left NULL manually; decide compute-from-current-metadata vs NULL.

REAL-RUN LEARNINGS (creating thing:7380581 + adopting 9):
- uploadFile AUTO-CLASSIFIES by mime type: PNG -> gallery image (sets default_image, not in file list); STL/zip -> downloadable file. One upload method for all.
- HARD per-file limit 250 MiB (262144000 bytes): "File is larger than maximum allowed size". ad5 must split oversized bundles (we split a 327MB zip by directory into two sub-250MiB zips) or skip+warn.
- update_thing PATCH accepts `tags` -> tags are patchable/drift-reconcilable (also license/category/description).
- Transient HTTP 500s on large uploads AND 429 rate-limiting both observed: throttle (~3s between calls) + exponential backoff/retry. Old v1 tooling used 3s sleeps.
- Zips are aggregate bundles (file_type=zip, not blueprint-backed).

title: Multi-Angle Thumbnail Viewing System

System generates 10 isometric-perspective angles (6 primary directions + 4 diagonal corners) during file scan using stl-thumb --cam-pos, combined into single sprite sheet PNG. title: [openforge-catalog] Every release PR conflicts because main is squash-merged
description: Observed on the 0.7.0 release: merging test into main as a squash leaves main with a commit test never saw, so the next test->main PR diffs from the pre-release merge base and GitHub reports conflicts across hundreds of files (388 on this one). The workaround each time is 'git merge -s ours origin/main' on test before opening the release PR, since main is always strictly behind in content. Options: enable merge commits on the repo so releases keep ancestry, or automate the ours-merge back into test right after each release. Compounded by GitHub not running the .beads merge driver, so .beads/issues.jsonl conflicts there even when a local merge is clean.

title: [guided builds] Stop the parser synthesising the base slot
description: Cleanup, not a fix, and not a blocker: it can land in parallel with the rest of the epic. openforge/data/metadata.py's apply_default_metadata appends a 'base' part to pieces with connection|openforge and the right shape, gated by build method (apply_openforge_wall requires build|separate wall and denies shape|floor, shape|base and build|s2w; apply_thick_wall requires build|thick wall plus component|wall). The data that produces is already correct: wall-on-tile walls have no base slot (0 of 397), nor do s2w walls (0 of 356) or s-system walls (0 of 41), and the wall-on-tile pieces that do carry one are 295 floors, 17 of them corners as well. All counts are over all 8,761 fixture records, .json and .yaml. The reason to remove it is Devon's, stated per method: within build|separate wall the slot and connection|openforge are the same fact (1,220 of 1,221; the exception carries shape|floor, which is_openforge_wall denies), and within build|thick wall likewise for the openforge walls carrying component|wall (87 of 100; the 13 without are wooden, slope and transition pieces). Across the catalog the tag alone does NOT imply a base — 4,368 records carry connection|openforge and only 2,455 of them have a base slot — so whatever replaces the slot must read the build method as well as the connection tag. Before removing: those three helpers are the only place in the repo that knows which pieces take bases under which method, so move that knowledge where the guide can read it. Verify by count afterwards: 2,499 base parts sit on 2,495 records, the three predicates account for 2,452 of those records, and the remaining 47 parts are authored and must survive — 40 in the s2w composition blueprints, 3 on dungeon_stone infinite-hallway pieces, and 4 in sewers.json where an authored slot sits beside a synthesised one, which is where the four duplicate base parts come from. Consumers that change meaning: src/utils/config-processing.ts, the blueprint page's compatible-bases UI, and collectDownloadUrls in src/utils/blueprint-utils.ts.
notes: Devon decided on 2026-09-19 that this lands LAST in the epic (after the guide page), not in parallel: the base rules are freshest then and it touches the blueprint page's base UI. Verification number after the parser change: 47 authored base parts on 47 records must survive (40 composition blueprints, 3 dungeon_stone infinite-hallway pieces, 4 sewers.json records whose authored slot sits beside a synthesised one).

title: [guided builds] Feature slots: doors, torches and the rest in a guide

title: Manifest schema + metadata assembler

Assembler builds the thing payload with defaults pulled from catalog Postgres blueprint records (name, description, tag hierarchy -> Thingiverse tags, category, license, images) and applies manifest overrides on top. Zero-manual-entry defaults, curated where it matters. Payload field names/shape finalized against the HAR contract.
notes: PRIOR ART (old v1 tool): bin/new.*.json templates were per-product-line defaults (openforge2, openlock, construction_kit, miniature, tools): license, category, tags, boilerplate description. Key design lesson: descriptions = per-thing content + SHARED BOILERPLATE FOOTER (Patreon/tutorials/catalog links) that changes over time. Model boilerplate as a shared block composed at assembly time (stored once, referenced by manifests), not baked into each manifest — enables bulk boilerplate updates via re-sync. title: [openforge-infra-frontend] CloudFront leaks the release sha on /admin and 404s SPA deep links

Fix in the catalog-cf module with CustomErrorResponse entries mapping 403/404 to /index.html with a 200, or a CloudFront Function that rewrites the path. title: [guided builds] Audit which pieces carry a base slot and why
description: ANSWERED during PR #238 review; closed, no code change needed. The question was whether the uneven distribution of base slots was deliberate or drift. It is deliberate and fully explained by (build method, component kind, connection|openforge). Over all 8,761 fixture records: under build|separate wall, 1,220 of the 1,221 openforge walls carry the slot and the single exception carries shape|floor as well as shape|wall, which is_openforge_wall denies outright; under build|thick wall, 87 of the 100 openforge walls carry it and the 13 without are wooden, slope and transition pieces, none carrying the component|wall that is_thick_wall requires; under build|wall on tile no wall carries one and 295 floors do; under build|s2w neither floors nor scanned walls carry one, and the only s2w records with a slot are the 40 composition blueprints, where the wall part declares fulfills: base; under build|s-system nothing carries one. The three predicates account for 2,452 of the 2,495 records with a base slot; the rest are authored — 40 composition blueprints, 3 dungeon_stone infinite-hallway pieces whose slot no predicate produces, and 4 sewers.json records carrying an authored slot beside the synthesised one. Detail is in docs/design/guided-builds.md.
notes: Correction to the close reason above: 'the base belongs to the floor' holds for build|wall on tile only. Under build|s2w no floor carries a slot either — the only s2w records with one are the 40 composition blueprints, where the wall part declares fulfills: base — and under build|s-system nothing carries one.
close_reason: Answered by evidence during PR #238 round-2 review, no code change needed. Base-slot presence is fully explained by (build method, component kind, connection|openforge): under build|separate wall, 1,220 of the 1,221 openforge walls carry the slot and the one exception is a shape|column|low piece, not a wall; under build|thick wall, 87 of the 100 openforge walls carry it and the 13 without are component|slope pieces, which is what is_thick_wall keys on; under wall on tile, s2w and s-system no wall carries one and the base belongs to the floor (295 wall-on-tile floors, 17 of them corners too). Not drift. Detail is in docs/design/guided-builds.md.

title: Capture HAR of Thingiverse SPA create/upload/edit flow and extract API contract
description: Devon captures a HAR (Network tab, preserve log, Fetch/XHR, 'Save all as HAR with content') of a complete flow: create draft thing, set name/description/tags/category/license, upload image, upload STL, replace the STL, delete a file, publish. HAR goes to scratchpad only — contains live JWT/refresh/cookies, never commit; rotate tokens after. From the HAR, extract and document: create-thing endpoint+payload, model-file upload mechanism (direct POST vs presigned URL — matters for Lambda), file object shape incl. hash field, metadata patch, and file delete. Also verify hash algorithm: hash the exact uploaded STL locally with MD5 and SHA-256 and match against the hash Thingiverse reports (Devon guesses SHA-256). Output: docs/thingiverse-api-v2-private.md contract doc.
notes: LARGELY SOLVED via v1 swagger (thingiverse.com/swagger/docs/openapi.yaml) + live probes. (1) HASH = content-MD5, confirmed empirically (downloaded a file, MD5 matches the File.hash field exactly). Catalog already stores file_md5 -> sync compares directly, NO SHA-256 needed (local_sha256 column is dead/harmless). (2) WRITE AUTH SOLVED: use the 'token' field from POST /v2/auth/login as Bearer (32-char opaque, devonjones-scoped id 47139), against api.thingiverse.com DIRECTLY (www origin is Cloudflare-challenged). The env THINGIVERSE_APP_TOKEN authenticates as Joaquin (wrong account) - do not use. (3) Write surface is v1: POST /things/ (create), POST /files/0/uploadFile (multipart -> {id}), POST /files/0/FinalizeFiles, GET /things/{id}/files (hash), POST /things/{id}/publish. Full contract: docs/thingiverse-api-v2-private.md. REMAINING: confirm POST /things/ payload on first real create; Devon notes v1 can't set all fields he wants (open request to Thingiverse for v2 write).
close_reason: Contract captured and validated end-to-end. Write auth (login token field, devonjones-scoped, api.thingiverse.com direct), file hash = MD5 (hex or base64 depending on upload path), write endpoints (v1: POST /things/, uploadFile+FinalizeFiles, publish), filename sanitization all documented in docs/thingiverse-api-v2-private.md and validated against thing:7364110 (31/31 STLs match catalog file_md5).

title: [openforge-catalog] Replace the production ALB with a Lambda function URL behind CloudFront
description: serverless-architecture-reviewer on PR #230: the ALB is ~16 USD/month of fixed cost per environment and exists only because CloudFront reaches it over HTTP. A function URL is per-invocation, HTTPS-only, and works as a CloudFront custom origin (https-only); /api/* routing moves to the CloudFront behavior. Blocker: aws_lambda_wsgi 0.0.6 only understands the ALB/API Gateway v1 event; a function URL needs a v2-capable adapter (e.g. apig-wsgi). Kept the ALB for parity on first deploy.
notes: Evidence 2026-09-18: staging GET /api/blueprints?limit=1 returns ALB 502 after ~8.7 s; the Lambda log shows 'LAMBDA_RUNTIME Failed to post handler success response. Http response code: 413' then Runtime.ExitError. ALB-invoked Lambda responses are capped at 1 MB; a function URL allows 6 MB (20 MB streaming). Also the endpoint ignores limit, or the unfiltered catalog exceeds 1 MB either way; check whether the frontend ever issues that request unfiltered.

title: [guided builds] Admin editor for guides
description: Deferred deliberately: guides start as repo fixtures so the shape can move cheaply. Once it has settled, an editor removes the git round-trip for content changes. Depends on the shape being stable, not on a date.
notes: Second thing from PR #239 review, for whoever writes guide editing: guide_key is a generated column (GENERATED ALWAYS AS document->>'key'), so a PATCH that rewrites the document RENAMES the guide, and a rename onto an occupied key raises psycopg UniqueViolation. The route has to turn that into a 409 rather than letting it become a 500. Verified against PG14 during review. This is better than the alternative it replaced (a stale guide_key silently disagreeing with the document), but it is now a deliberate decision the editing UI has to make: either refuse to change a guide's key, or handle the collision. Also noted: the DDL guards presence (NOT NULL) and agreement, but not shape — {"key": 42} would store '42' via raw SQL. Every writer goes through validate_guide_document, whose url_key pattern rejects that, so this is only reachable by bypassing the loader.

title: Design R2 storage structure for multi-angle thumbnails
description: Define R2 storage using SPRITE SHEET approach: Generate single PNG containing all 10 isometric-perspective angles in a grid layout (5x2 or 2x5 grid). Angles: 6 primary isometric views (front-iso, back-iso, left-iso, right-iso, top-iso, bottom-iso) + 4 diagonal corners (NE, NW, SE, SW). All maintain 3/4 perspective for depth, not flat orthographic. File naming: {model_id}_angles.png or {md5}_angles.png. Each angle occupies equal-sized tile. Store grid layout metadata in database. One file per model instead of 10 separate files.
close_reason: Completed: Created comprehensive design document (docs/sprite-sheet-storage-design.md) specifying R2 storage structure, sprite layout (2x5 grid, 512x512 tiles), 10 camera angles, path structure (sprites/{md5[:6]}/{md5}.png), and integration strategy.

title: Update stl-thumb integration to generate 8+ camera angles

(2) 10 angles by rotating camera around model: Front-iso (default: 2,-4,2), Back-iso (~-2,4,2), Left-iso (~-4,-2,2), Right-iso (~4,2,2), Top-iso (higher z, maintain angle), Bottom-iso (lower z), plus 4 diagonal corners (NE, NW, SE, SW at ~4,±2,2 variants). FOV auto-adjusts. (3) Combine all 10 into SPRITE SHEET PNG using PIL/Pillow (5x2 grid). (4) Store camera coords and grid metadata. Generate during file scan.

title: [tags] tag_search pagination is unreliable when blueprint names collide
description: Found during PR #239 round 5. tag_search_blueprints paginates with 'bp2.blueprint_name > (SELECT blueprint_name FROM blueprints WHERE id = next)' — a comparison on blueprint_name alone. 159 names in the catalog are shared by two or more records (mostly bases, e.g. plain#base+curved+radial...), so at a page boundary that lands on a duplicated name the next page can skip or repeat rows. PR #239 added the id as a tiebreaker to both ORDER BY clauses, which makes the ordering total and the LIMIT deterministic, but the pagination predicate still compares only the name, so the keyset is not aligned with the sort key. The fix is a compound comparison — (blueprint_name, id) > (name_of_cursor, id_of_cursor) — which is a change to the paging contract and deserves its own PR. Also worth doing at the same time: test_tag_search_tags and test_tag_search_blueprint_images pass bare tag strings, which _query_tags_include silently drops, so both assert only that a record exists rather than that the search finds it by tag.
notes: Also in scope, found in PR #239 round 6: tag_search_blueprint_start_count has the same strict comparison on blueprint_name alone, so paging.start_count is wrong when names collide — measured start_count 10 where the true offset in the (name, id) order is 7. Fix it with the same compound comparison as the next/previous predicates. Note the ordering itself is now total: PR #239 added the id to both ORDER BY clauses, so the rows a boundary loses are deterministic rather than varying run to run. Measured before and after over 40 rows with 8 names x 5: identical counts either way (28 returned, 0 repeats, 12 never shown), so this bug is unchanged in kind, not worsened.

title: [guided builds] Retire the s2w composition blueprints once the wall guide covers them
description: Devon's decision on 2026-09-19: the wall guide replaces the 40 hand-authored s2w composition blueprints (the 20 blueprints.s2w.*.yaml fixtures, type: blueprint) rather than living beside them, so s2w has one source instead of two that drift. What retiring them involves: they are type: blueprint records so they appear in blueprint search (models=false), and the blueprint page renders their parts via src/components/blueprint/config-section.tsx; decide whether to deprecate them (there is a deprecation mechanism with successor_id) or delete the fixtures, and what a link to one should do afterwards.

title: [guided builds] Author the wall guide
description: Content work, with Devon. Three methods only — build|s2w, build|wall on tile, build|separate wall; Devon decided on 2026-09-19 that build|thick wall and build|s-system are not in this guide. For each: the roles it needs, the query per role, the recommended part, the refinements and their when: conditions, and the prose. Decisions already made: a guide never recommends a damaged piece by default, so the role queries deny component|collapsed, component|broken, component|collapsing_blocks and the four ruined textures (deny is an exact match, so each is listed; every component|collapsed|* piece carries the bare parent, so one entry covers that family). The s2w content is copied from the 40 composition blueprints, which already encode it: floor = build|s2w + shape|floor|wall (88 tiles), wall = build|separate wall + component|wall (there is no straight s2w wall — 219 of the 220 candidates are corner halves), base = shape|base|wall + build|s2w; and their single-piece variants add connection|openforge to the wall and declare fulfills: base, which the guide expresses by listing no base role for that option. Those compositions are then retired (openforge_catalog-yan). Other facts to author against: no floor tile carries build|separate wall (of 1,319 floor tiles, 295 are wall on tile, 88 s2w, 936 untagged), no base carries build|wall on tile, and a role-level deny is absolute because composition is a union — the floor role cannot deny shape|wall without removing the s2w combined tiles, so the methods that want a plain floor deny it in their own option. Still open for Devon: ranking within the intact pieces, since prefer is hand-ordered and the tie-break is filename order. Illustrations are at /mnt/d/OpenForge/Sets/ in 17 directories, but the naming cannot be trusted to give the method: the 47 dungeon_stone.s2w.*.png files live in dungeon_stone.separate_wall.primary_wall/, so images are picked per option by hand.
notes: Corrections from PR #238 rounds 4-5, to use when authoring: (1) the 40 s2w composition blueprints are not uniform — 32 are wall/floor/base, four are column/floor/base and four add left wall and right wall; their base part denies build|s2w in 20 and requires it in 17; (2) which part a base sits under is the method's choice — under build|separate wall 1,220 of the 1,221 openforge walls carry a base slot and none of the 115 floors does, under build|wall on tile it is the 295 floors and no wall, under build|s2w no floor does and the composites put fulfills: base on the wall part, and under build|s-system nothing carries one, so the wall guide wants two roles (floor-base and wall-base) rather than one; (3) no base record carries build|wall on tile at all — bases are 761 separate wall, 292 thick wall, 95 s2w and 821 with no build tag, so a wall-on-tile floor's base is an untagged one, which is exactly what apply_openforge_floor asks for; (4) a bare shape|base query matches 1,874 candidates, so every base role needs a prefer list or the recommendation is whatever sorts first by name.
